findings: all 82 are 'folded' (negative determinant); none is collapsed, non-finite or unmapped
every one lies in a vertical strip near the right sensor edge: source x 7992-8155 of 8256 (96.8-98.8% of the width), station x 7969-8193, across the full height

only the x derivative is wrong: d(source x)/d(station x) is -0.01 to -205, while d(source y)/d(station y) stays 0.857-1.011. Values far below -1 over a 1 px central difference are a jump in the mapping, not a smooth fold
22 of the 82 have no native residual displacement, so the jump is not only from the displacement field
hypothesis_unverified: FocusSourceSampling::mapping (stitching/focus_layers.rs) switches between the global inverse and per-band local inverses; a band candidate is dropped once its normalized source x leaves [min-0.02, max+0.02]. A vertical-edge / long-edge consensus band ending near the right sensor edge would make the source mapping discontinuous in x exactly in this strip. Band ranges were not exported, so this is not yet proven
implications: the langyuan scale=1 density bypass (invalid_native_jacobian_probes) comes from a source-sampling discontinuity in a narrow edge strip, not from a real fold of the station geometry

C7 / C2: a residual-aware density planner would hit the same discontinuity; it needs either a continuous band transition in production sampling (changes pixels) or an explicit, recorded exclusion of such probes (contract change)
